**Southwest Water Authority (SWA)**

---

**1. Introduction**

This report summarises the compliance performance of Southwest Water Authority (SWA) for the calendar year 2023. It covers water quality standards, supply interruptions, environmental permit compliance, and the handling of incidents and fines. The report is submitted to the relevant regulatory bodies and senior management for review and action planning.

Southwest Water Authority has_region_code R12. Record status: current. This code applies to all operational sites, supply zones, and reporting units referenced within this document. All compliance ratings and incident references in this report are to be read in conjunction with the R12 regional framework.

The reporting period saw a mixed compliance picture. While the majority of routine water quality sampling returned results within prescribed limits, the year was marked by two significant pollution events and an extended period of supply interruption in the eastern supply zone. These incidents have driven the improvement priorities set out in Section 6.

---

---

**3. Incident Summary and Fines**

**3.1 Pollution Incidents**

Two pollution incidents were recorded during 2023. Both were categorised as Category 2 (significant) under the environmental impact assessment framework.

**3.2 Supply Interruption Events**
**3.2 Supply Interruption Events**

Three supply interruption events were logged during the reporting year, all of which were reported to the Drinking Water Inspectorate in accordance with Regulation 29(5) of the Water Supply (Water Quality) Regulations 2016. A summary of each event is provided below.

**Event 1 – Eastvale, 14 June 2023**
A burst on a 300 mm trunk main at the junction of Mill Lane and the A417 resulted in a loss of supply to approximately 1,150 properties for a period of 6 hours 40 minutes. The event was caused by ground movement following nearby excavation works by a third-party contractor. Booster tankering was deployed from 09:15 BST; supplies were fully restored by 15:55 BST. A precautionary boil water notice was not considered necessary as pressure was maintained in the network throughout, and subsequent sample results confirmed no deterioration in water quality. The contractor has accepted liability, and their insurers have reimbursed the company for direct costs incurred. Customer compensation payments were issued automatically under the Guaranteed Standards Scheme.

**Event 2 – Westfield, 2 October 2023**
A loss of supply affected 87 properties on the Highfield Estate for 3 hours 20 minutes following a fault at the Westfield booster pumping station (PS 14/03). The fault was traced to a failed variable speed drive on pump No. 2, which has since been replaced. The station is now operating on the original duty pump with the standby pump fully functional. An internal investigation concluded that the failure was consistent with the age of the unit (installed 2008) and that routine condition monitoring had not identified the deterioration in the drive components. Maintenance intervals for all variable speed drives at Westfield PS have been revised from annual to six-monthly, effective from January 2024.

**Event 3 – North Moor, 18 November 2023**
A loss of pressure and subsequent supply interruption affected 42 properties in the hamlet of Lower Birkham. The event was caused by a blockage in a 150 mm distribution main, attributed to an accumulation of sediment following a period of high turbidity in the raw water source. The main was flushed and scoured on 19 November, and the network has operated normally since. No water quality failures were recorded in samples taken after the event.

**3.3 Enforcement Actions**

The Company received two enforcement notices during 2023, both of which are currently being addressed. Details are as follows:

**Notice 1 – Eastvale WTW (Manganese)**
In September 2023, the Drinking Water Inspectorate issued a Notice of Intent to serve an Enforcement Order in respect of the elevated manganese levels identified at Eastvale WTW. The notice requires the Company to submit a detailed action plan for the installation of additional treatment capacity, specifically for the removal of dissolved manganese. A revised action plan was submitted to the Inspectorate on 15 December 2023 and is currently under review. The Company anticipates that the full installation will be completed by Q3 2024, ahead of the deadline specified in the notice. Interim measures, including enhanced dosing of potassium permanganate and increased frequency of filter backwashing, have been implemented to mitigate the risk of further exceedances.

**Notice 2 – Westfield Distribution Network (Iron)**
In November 2023, the Inspectorate issued a formal caution in respect of the iron failures recorded in the Westfield distribution network. The caution relates to the Company's failure to maintain adequate corrosion control measures. A programme of targeted mains flushing and the installation of a new orthophosphate dosing rig at Westfield WTW has been initiated. The dosing rig is expected to be operational by the end of Q1 2024. The Company has also commenced a condition assessment of the cast iron mains in the affected area to identify sections requiring relining or replacement.

2. Methodology

Data was extracted from the monthly zone returns (source: Network Maintenance Team, Zone Demand
and Performance Data). The metrics reviewed were:

- Average daily demand (ML/d)
- Leakage rate (litres per property per day)
- Pressure at critical points (m)
- Pumping station energy (kWh/ML)
- Water quality compliance (%)

Normalisation was applied to account for differences in zone size (number of properties) and
seasonal weather effects. The seasonal adjustment used a five-year rolling average (2018–2022)
as the baseline. March 2023 was notably dry, which affected several zones; the adjustment for
March was based on the 2018–2022 March baseline only.

**3.2 Supply Interruption Events**

Three supply interruption events were logged during the reporting year, all of which were reported to the Drinking Water Inspectorate in accordance with Regulation 29(5) of the Water Supply (Water Quality) Regulations 2016. A summary of each event is provided below.

**Event 1 – Eastvale, 14 June 2023**
A burst on a 300 mm trunk main at the junction of Mill Lane and the A417 resulted in a loss of supply to approximately 1,150 properties for a period of 6 hours 40 minutes. The event was caused by ground movement following nearby excavation works by a third-party contractor. Booster tankering was deployed from 09:15 BST; supplies were fully restored by 15:55 BST. A precautionary boil water notice was not considered necessary as pressure was maintained in the network throughout, and subsequent sample results confirmed no deterioration in water quality. The contractor has accepted liability, and their insurers have reimbursed the company for direct costs incurred. Customer compensation payments were issued automatically under the Guaranteed Standards Scheme.

**Event 2 – Westfield, 2 October 2023**
A loss of supply affected 87 properties on the Highfield Estate for 3 hours 20 minutes following a fault at the Westfield booster pumping station (PS 14/03). The fault was traced to a failed variable speed drive on pump No. 2, which has since been replaced. The station is now operating on the original duty pump with the standby pump fully functional. An internal investigation concluded that the failure was consistent with the age of the unit (installed 2008) and that routine condition monitoring had not identified the deterioration in the drive components. Maintenance intervals for all variable speed drives at Westfield PS have been revised from annual to six-monthly, effective from January 2024.

**Event 3 – North Moor, 18 November 2023**
A loss of pressure and subsequent supply interruption affected 42 properties in the hamlet of Lower Birkham. The event was caused by a blockage in a 150 mm distribution main, attributed to an accumulation of sediment following a period of high turbidity in the raw water source. The main was flushed and scoured on 19 November, and the network has operated normally since. No water quality failures were recorded in samples taken after the event.

**3.3 Enforcement Actions**

The Company received two enforcement notices during 2023, both of which are currently being addressed. Details are as follows:

**Notice 1 – Eastvale WTW (Manganese)**
In September 2023, the Drinking Water Inspectorate issued a Notice of Intent to serve an Enforcement Order in respect of the elevated manganese levels identified at Eastvale WTW. The notice requires the Company to submit a detailed action plan for the installation of additional treatment capacity, specifically for the removal of dissolved manganese. A revised action plan was submitted to the Inspectorate on 15 December 2023 and is currently under review. The Company anticipates that the full installation will be completed by Q3 2024, ahead of the deadline specified in the notice. Interim measures, including enhanced dosing of potassium permanganate and increased frequency of filter backwashing, have been implemented to mitigate the risk of further exceedances.

**Notice 2 – Westfield Distribution Network (Iron)**
In November 2023, the Inspectorate issued a formal caution in respect of the iron failures recorded in the Westfield distribution network. The caution relates to the Company's failure to maintain adequate corrosion control measures. A programme of targeted mains flushing and the installation of a new orthophosphate dosing rig at Westfield WTW has been initiated. The dosing rig is expected to be operational by the end of Q1 2024. The Company has also commenced a condition assessment of the cast iron mains in the affected area to identify sections requiring relining or replacement.

For 2023, the regional average daily demand across all ten zones was 14.1 ML/d. Bristol's average
was 21.6 ML/d, which is 53% above the regional figure. The next highest zone was Exeter at
15.2 ML/d. Bristol also had the highest maximum output at 25.7 ML/d (see WTW table, March data).

The normalised demand metric used throughout this review is the z-score, calculated as
(zone value – regional mean) / regional standard deviation. A zone is flagged as an outlier when
its z-score exceeds 2.0 for two or more consecutive months. Bristol exceeded this threshold in
eight of the twelve months.

2. Methodology

Data was extracted from the monthly zone returns (source: Network Maintenance Team, Zone Demand
and Performance Data). The metrics reviewed were:

- Average daily demand (ML/d)
- Leakage rate (litres per property per day)
- Pressure at critical points (m)
- Pumping station energy (kWh/ML)
- Water quality compliance (%)

Normalisation was applied to account for differences in zone size (number of properties) and
seasonal weather effects. The seasonal adjustment used a five-year rolling average (2018–2022)
as the baseline. March 2023 was notably dry, which affected several zones; the adjustment for
March was based on the 2018–2022 March baseline only.

3. Outlier Identification – Bristol Distribution Zone

Priya Nair identified_outlier_zone_2023 as Bristol Distribution Zone in the spreadsheet after
reviewing the December data. The z-scores for Bristol exceeded the 2.0 threshold in every month
from March onwards, with the exception of June (z = 1.8) and September (z = 1.9). The highest
z-score was in July (z = 3.4). No other zone had a z-score above 2.0 for more than two months.

Priya Nair identified_outlier_zone_2023 as Bristol Distribution Zone in the spreadsheet. Record status: historical.

4. Contributing Factors – Bristol Zone

The following factors were considered in the review:

- Population growth: Bristol zone added approximately 1,200 properties during 2023 (planning
  records indicate 1,180 completions). This is the highest growth of any zone.
- Leakage: The leakage rate for Bristol averaged 12.4 litres per property per day for the year,
  compared with the regional average of 9.8. Leakage peaked in February at 14.1.
- Industrial demand: Two large industrial customers (a brewery and a logistics hub) are
  supplied from the Bristol zone. Their combined demand averaged 4.2 ML/d in 2023, up from

- Pressure management: Pressure at the Bristol PS outlet was reduced by 0.5 bar in April as a
  trial to reduce leakage. This had no measurable effect on demand.

**Maintenance Work Log 2023-2024**
**Network Maintenance Team – Annual Summary & Review**
**Period Covered: 01/01/2023 – 31/12/2023 (with Q1 2024 notes)**
**Compiled by: R. Davies, Maintenance Supervisor**
**Date of Summary: 12/01/2024**

---

**1. OVERVIEW**

This summary covers maintenance activities undertaken by the Network Maintenance Team across the municipal water network for the 2023 calendar year. It includes response times, job completion rates, backlog trends, and notable issues encountered. The log continues from the detailed daily entries recorded throughout the year and provides a consolidated view for management review.

The team consists of 8 full-time technicians, 2 apprentices, and a part-time administrative support officer. The network area covers 14 pumping stations, 6 service reservoirs, 3 water treatment works (WTW), and approximately 480 km of distribution mains.

---

**2. JOB VOLUME AND COMPLETION**

A total of 1,247 maintenance jobs were logged during 2023. This compares with 1,182 in 2022, an increase of 5.5%. Of these:

- **1,106 jobs (88.7%)** were completed and closed (CMP).
- **89 jobs (7.1%)** were still open (OPN) at year end.
- **52 jobs (4.2%)** were cancelled (CNX) – mostly due to duplicate reports or no fault found on arrival.

The average monthly job count was 104, with the busiest month being July (132 jobs) and the quietest being December (81 jobs). The increase in workload is attributed to the ageing infrastructure in the Greenhill area and the unusually dry summer, which led to more demand on pumps and boosters.

---

**3. RESPONSE TIMES**

Response time is defined as the time from report receipt to team arrival on site. The target is 2 hours for emergency jobs and 24 hours for routine jobs. Average response times for 2023:

- **Emergency jobs (flooding, no water, major leak):** 42 minutes average (target 60 mins). Best month: March (35 mins). Worst month: July (58 mins) due to high call volume.
- **Routine jobs:** 5 hrs 15 mins average (target 24 hrs). Best month: November (3 hrs 40 mins). Worst month: July (8 hrs 10 mins).

The team consistently met the emergency target, with the only exception being a 3-day period in late July when two technicians were off sick and one was on annual leave, causing delays of up to 1 hr 50 mins on emergency call-outs.

**1. Minutes of Previous Meeting (15 Jan 2024)**
The minutes of the meeting held on 15 January were accepted as a correct record, aside from one amendment: Action 15/12 (P. Hargreaves) regarding the valve chamber survey at Eastgate should read “survey complete by 2 Feb” rather than “survey complete by 26 Jan”. The amended date is reflected in the action log below.

**2. Matters Arising**
- Action 24/03 (L. Chen) – SCADA alarm threshold review for the Lowfield PS telemetry: still in progress. L. Chen reported that the alarm historian is showing a higher than expected number of nuisance alarms on the night shift, and she is cross-referencing these against the site log before adjusting the deadbands. Revised completion date 29 Jan.
- Action 24/04 (J. Broadbent) – Updated sampling schedule for the Raw Water intake at Merrow WTW: closed. New schedule circulated 19 Jan and posted on the noticeboard in the control room.
- Action 24/05 (R. Tesh) – Replacement of the duty pump seal at Eastgate PS: closed. Seal replaced 18 Jan; pump returned to service at 14:30 and has been running within normal vibration limits since.

**3. Operational Report – Week Commencing 15 Jan 2024**
M. Okafor summarised the week’s performance. Treated water output averaged 41.2 Ml/d across the three works, slightly below the seasonal target of 42.0 Ml/d. The shortfall is attributed mainly to the planned maintenance outage at Merrow WTW on 17 Jan (08:00–16:00) for the replacement of a filter air-scour valve. No supply interruptions were reported to customers.

Network pressures remained within the statutory minimum at all monitored points. The lowest recorded pressure was 22.4 m at the Hatherley Road monitoring point on the morning of 19 Jan, which is above the 15 m minimum but lower than the typical 26–28 m for that location. P. Hargreaves noted that this may be linked to the overnight tank level at the Hatherley service resevoir (note: spelling as per site log) dropping to 68% before refilling. He will review the inlet valve control settings.

Water quality compliance for the week was 100% for all regulatory samples taken. J. Broadbent reported one non-regulatory sample from the Limehouse Road dead-end main that showed a marginal increase in turbidity (0.9 NTU) after a burst repair on 16 Jan. Flushing was carried out on 18 Jan and a resample on 20 Jan returned a normal result (0.2 NTU). No further action required.

In the meeting minutes, Sarah Whitfield approval_date_for_budget_2024 is 2024-04-12. Record status: historical.

**4. Finance – Budget 2024**
A. Voss joined the meeting for this item to present the draft operational budget for the 2024/25 financial year. The draft includes a 4.2% increase in chemical costs (driven by the new coagulation dosing regime at Merrow WTW), a 6% increase in electricity charges per the new supply contract, and a provision for the planned replacement of the standby generator at Lowfield PS.

The draft budget was discussed in detail, particularly the provision for the generator replacement, which is currently estimated at £185k including civils works. R. Tesh queried whether the generator had been included in the 10-year asset renewal plan; it was confirmed that it had been flagged as a high-risk asset in the 2023 condition assessment.

S. Whitfield noted that she would review the draft budget and provide final approval. The budget was not approved at this meeting; it was agreed that the final version would be circulated for a decision at the next scheduled meeting. The chair confirmed that she would hold the approval until the finance sign-off had been received from the regional office.

**Operations Meeting Minutes – Week Commencing 22 January 2024**

**Meeting 05/24 – Held 25 January 2024, 09:30, Operations Control Room**

**Attendees:** S. Whitfield (Chair), R. Tesh, P. Hargreaves, J. Broadbent, M. Okafor, L. Dunning, A. Voss (Finance, item 4 only)
**Apologies:** C. Nair, D. Fellows

**1. Minutes of Previous Meeting (18 Jan 2024)**

The minutes of the meeting held on 18 January were agreed as a true record. Matters arising were noted as follows:

- Action 04/24-12 (P. Hargreaves – review inlet valve control settings at Hatherley service resevoir): In progress. A site visit was carried out on 23 Jan; initial observations indicate the level sensor may be drifting. Further data logging required. Revised completion date: 01 Feb.
- Action 04/24-14 (J. Broadbent – confirm flushing complete at Limehouse Road): Closed. Resample result 0.2 NTU received on 20 Jan.

**2. Network Operations Report – Week 19 Jan to 25 Jan**

P. Hargreaves presented the weekly network summary.

Pressure management:
- The Hatherley Road pressure issue reported last week has not recurred. Pressure has remained between 24.1 m and 27.6 m over the past seven days. The overnight tank level at Hatherley service resevoir has held above 82% since 21 Jan.
- A new low-pressure query was received from a customer on Priory Close on 23 Jan. A pressure logger was installed the same day. Initial 24-hour data shows minimum pressure of 12.8 m at the customer boundary, which is below the 15 m minimum threshold. The area is fed from the Priory Close PS, which has a history of pump cycling issues.
- M. Okafor noted that the pumps at Priory Close PS were replaced in 2019 and are due a routine service. The service is currently scheduled for March. R. Tesh asked whether the service could be brought forward given the pressure query. P. Hargreaves agreed to contact the service provider to check availability. Action 05/24-01 (P. Hargreaves, due 29 Jan).

Burst activity:
- Three bursts were attended during the week. Two were minor leaks on service connections (no supply interruption). The third was a 100 mm main burst on the corner of Mill Lane and Station Approach on 22 Jan. The burst was reported at 06:40 and the water was isolated by 07:15. Estimated customers affected: 45. Repairs were completed by 15:30 the same day. A sample was taken after reinstatement; results are awaited.
- J. Broadbent noted that the Mill Lane burst was on a section of 100 mm uPVC main installed in 1987. This section has been flagged in the renewal programme but is not due for replacement until 2026/27. He asked whether the burst history should be reviewed to consider bringing the replacement forward. R. Tesh agreed to review the burst history for this section and report back at the next meeting. Action 05/24-02 (R. Tesh, due 01 Feb).

Reservoir levels:
- All service reservoirs finished the week above 75% capacity. The lowest level recorded was at Hatherley service resevoir (78% on the morning of 24 Jan), which is within normal operating range for this time of year.

**3. Water Quality**

J. Broadbent reported:
- Regulatory compliance for the week was 100% for all samples taken.
- One customer complaint regarding taste and odour was received from a property on Elm Grove on 21 Jan. A sample was taken on 22 Jan. The sample showed no detectable issues; the result was within normal parameters. The complaint is being closed as unsubstantiated.
- The turbidity result from the Mill Lane burst repair is still pending. The laboratory has confirmed the sample was received and results are expected by 28 Jan.
